jobs.title: Case Supervisor (Practicum Student)
jobs.description:
This exciting opportunity is designed for individuals who are actively completing coursework to become a BCBA and are accruing practicum hours. Struggling to get opportunities that count toward your unrestricted hours? Looking for a role where you can get paid while building the clinical skills needed to become a BCBA? This role is for you.

The Case Supervisor role is intended to help you develop the foundational skills needed to become a successful BCBA, while receiving structured supervision, coaching, and hands-on clinical experience. This role reports to the Local Clinical Trainer, who is a BCBA, at your assigned clinic.

This role is part of Soar’s Apex Program
, our enhanced development pathway for future BCBAs. Apex is designed to elevate how we develop and support Case Supervisors as they build clinical readiness, accrue practicum hours, and pursue a long-term career as a BCBA.

The Case Supervisor
role is designed for practicum students who are earlier in their BCBA journey and are generally more than 6–9 months away from completing requirements to become a BCBA. In this Apex Program, you will receive enhanced development, ongoing supervision, clinical training, and opportunities to build community with other Case Supervisors across Soar. This role has the opportunity for promotion to Lead Case Supervisor when you are within 6 months of testing!

Highlights of the Role

Base pay: $22.50 - $27.00/hour. The initial offer hourly pay will be between $22.50 - $23.75.
Serve as a case supervisor for 1-3 client cases (10 paid unrestricted hours/week), learning and practicing the key skills to become a high-quality BCBA. This is a full-time hourly, position.
Receive dedicated supervision, training, and feedback from your Local Clinical Trainer and other BCBAs in your center
Participate in Apex learning and development opportunities
Build clinical skills through exposure to ESDM, interdisciplinary care, family guidance, assessment, and behavior intervention planning
Join a supportive community of future BCBAs across Soar
Work in a culture that lives out our values: high expectations, collaboration, and fun

Job Responsibilities

As a Case Supervisor, you will:

Serve as a case supervisor for client cases, with scope determined by center needs, clinical readiness, and program progress
Accrue paid unrestricted hours through client programming, supervision, family guidance, assessment, and other BCBA-aligned responsibilities
Update client goals and programming using Soar’s electronic data collection platform
Provide support and supervision to RBTs, with coaching and feedback from BCBAs
Participate in ESDM-specific trainings to grow your clinical skillset
Learn to develop Behavior Intervention Plans using approaches such as Practical Functional Assessment and Skill-Based Treatment
Support family treatment guidance meetings using Soar’s in-house curriculum
Assist with assessments and reassessments for clients, including exposure to tools such as the Vineland, QABF, FAST, and ESDM Curriculum Checklist
Receive coaching and feedback from your Local Clinical Trainer, Partner Clinician, and other BCBAs in your clinic
Participate in interdisciplinary collaboration with Speech-Language Pathologists, Occupational Therapists, Psychologists, and other members of the integrated care team
Provide direct client therapy as part of your full-time role, with the weekly mix of direct therapy and unrestricted activities determined by center needs and program progress

Qualifications

Must be enrolled in or recently completed a Master’s program in ABA or a related field that meets BCBA coursework requirements
You must be at least in your second semester of your master’s or certificate program

Actively accruing practicum hours toward BCBA certification
Demonstrated ability to build rapport and trust with children and families
Emerging skills in case conceptualization, client programming, and clinical planning
Emerging skills in coaching and supporting RBTs
Strong desire to learn, grow, and receive feedback
Commitment to Soar’s mission and values
Interest in growing into a future BCBA role

What We Offer

A mission deeply focused on care quality for children and their families
Competitive compensation package commensurate with experience
Quality medical, dental, and vision plans
A company 401(k) with company contribution
Generous paid time off, including holidays and personal days
Paid unrestricted hours
Structured supervision and clinical development
Opportunities for professional growth and advancement within a growing organization

Applications for this position will be accepted on a rolling deadline.

jobs.title: Case Manager
jobs.description:
Job Summary

This position is located in the Case Management Services division of the District of Columbia Department of Corrections (DOC), Central Detention Facility (CDF/DC Jail) and Correctional Treatment Facility (CTF). The DOC facilities serve as points of entry for persons who have been arraigned and committed for incarceration by the Superior Court of the District of Columbia the U.S. District Court, and any detainments under the authority of the U.S. Marshall Service.

Case Management Services is responsible for the development of a planned program of institutional activities designed to meet the varied demands, individual needs and abilities of the inmates in DOC custody.

Duties And Responsibilities

CS-09

Provides management, guidance, and evaluation of assigned caseload. Conducts intake interviews with newly admitted inmates in assigned area to obtain pertinent data, and to orient inmates to the institutional rules, regulations, procedures and program opportunities. Conducts Risk and Needs assessment in order to help inmates to identify goals they want to achieve; and during incarceration, help inmates connect with relevant community service providers.

Gathers information from new inmates within 72 hours of admission in order to conduct classification to determine the custody level of the inmates according to their respective charges. Reclassifies inmates every 90 days to ensure the correct classification/custody level is maintained. Recommends programming identified for pre-release inmates that are designed to assist with readjustment to life in the community. Refers inmates to therapeutic services, including but not limited to, stress management, life skills, substance use and anger management programs, while still incarcerated.

CS-11

Develops and implements a planned program of institutional activities designed to meet the varied demands, individual needs, and abilities of an assigned caseload of inmates. Provides management, guidance, and evaluation of assigned caseload. Prepares and when required, presents reports based on observed inmate behavior, conformity to jail policies and procedures, and other evaluative outcomes. Identifies and assesses significant factors or variables in the inmate’s history that may have contributed to criminal behavior.

Considers and evaluates such factors as educational background, family relationships, socioeconomic factors prior to arrest history, substance abuse and where applicable, physical/mental status, etc. Develops a program designed to meet/challenge the inmate during the period of incarceration, with the goal of rehabilitation in thinking, behavior, and outlook. Makes recommendations annually regarding changes to inmate programs based on the review and reclassification of inmates assigned to caseloads.

Qualifications And Education

Degree: Behavioral or social science; or related disciplines appropriate to the position.

OR

Combination of education and experience that provided the applicant with knowledge of one or more of the behavioral or social sciences equivalent to a major in the field.

OR

Four years of appropriate experience that demonstrated that the applicant has acquired knowledge of one or more of the behavioral or social sciences equivalent to a major in the field.

In addition, this position requires Specialized Experience that equipped the applicant with the particular knowledge, skills, and abilities to perform successfully the duties of the position, and that is typically in or related to the work of the position to be filled. To be creditable, one (1) year of specialized experience must have been equivalent to at least the next lower grade level in the normal line of progression.

LICENSES AND CERTIFICATIONS

None.

WORKING CONDITIONS/ENVIRONMENT

Work is performed in a Detention Facility office setting.

Other Significant Facts

Note: This position will be filled at the grade CS-09 or CS-11 level.

Tour of Duty:
Monday - Friday 8:15am to 4:45pm

Pay Plan, Series and Grade:
CS-0101-9

Promotion Potential:
Grade 9 has Promotion Potential to Grade 11.

Grade 11 has No known Promotion Potential.

Duration of Appointment:
Career Service-Term Appt.

Collective Bargaining Unit:
This position may be covered by a collective bargaining agreement.

Position Designation:
This position is designated as a Safety Sensitive
position and is subject to mandatory pre-employment and periodic Criminal Background Checks and Traffic Records Checks (as applicable). This position is also subject to mandatory pre-employment and random Drug and Alcohol Testing. In this position, you may be disqualified from employment based on the presence of marijuana in test results, even if you possess a medical card authorizing the use of medical marijuana.

Essential Position Designation:
This position has been designated as Essential
employee position under the provisions of District Personnel Manual, Chapter 12. As such, individuals in this position may be required in emergency situations to perform crucial duties that are vital to the continuity of medical facilities, public safety, emergency services, and/or other crucial operations. These duties may be performed when the government is closed or when most employees are dismissed early. Employees designated as essential shall be required to be at work regardless of the emergency situation declared.

A TB Test is required prior to entry on duty.

Residency Preference:
When claiming residency preference, you are required, and must agree in writing, to maintain bona fide District residency for a period of seven (7) consecutive years from the effective date of employment. You will be required to present documents (proof) to show District residency and failure to maintain bona-fide District residency for the seven-year (7) period will result in forfeiture of employment

Develop customer and employee virtual training programs along with the Education Development Specialist, Siemens training center instructors and clinical education team members and maintain a database of all training materials.
Consult with other trainers, managers, and leadership to ensure training sessions and business needs are in sync

Detailed knowledge of the latest Siemens imaging systems and applications
Proficient computer skills, Microsoft Office Suite and instructional software
Strong organizational skills including establishing and meeting timelines and schedules
Able to multitask, prioritize, and manage time efficiently
Able to analyze problems and strategize for better solutions

jobs.description:
Who We Are:

The Micronesia Conservation Trust (MCT) is a non-governmental, non-profit conservation finance organization established to provide sustainable financing for conservation and community development across Micronesia. MCT has a 24-year institutional history and serves as a regional hub for conservation finance across the Federated States of Micronesia (FSM), Palau, the Republic of the Marshall Islands, and the broader Micronesian sub-region.

Under an agreement with the United Nations Development Program (UNDP), MCT has been contracted to serve as the National Host Institution (NHI) for the Global Environment Facility (GEF) Small Grants Program (SGP) in the FSM. The SGP supports civil society organizations and community groups to implement projects that address global environmental challenges – including biodiversity loss, land degradation, climate change, and threats to international waters – in ways that enhance local livelihoods and community well-being.

What We Can Achieve Together:

The Small Grants Programme Manager is responsible for the effective, transparent, and accountable
implementation of the GEF SGP in the FSM. The Manager will ensure that grant resources are directed to eligible, high-impact projects; that grantee organizations are adequately supported throughout the project cycle; and that program results are documented and reported in accordance with UNDP/GEF requirements.

We’re Looking for You:

MCT is seeking to recruit a qualified and experienced Small Grants Program Manager to lead the day-to-day implementation of the SGP-FSM. This role will be based in Chuuk State and will work closely with MCT leadership, a national technical review body, UNDP, GEF, and community stakeholders across the FSM.

What You’ll Bring:

Bachelor’s degree in environmental science, natural resource management, development studies, public administration, or a related field. A Master’s degree is an advantage.
Minimum of five (5) years of professional experience in program or project management, preferably in grant-making, conservation, or community development.
Demonstrated experience in grants management, including proposal review, due diligence, contracting, disbursement tracking, and reporting.
Experience working with or within civil society organizations, government agencies, or international development organizations in the Pacific Islands region.
Strong written and oral communication skills in English; proficiency in a Micronesian language is an advantage.
Demonstrated proficiency in financial management and basic accounting practices related to grant administration.
Ability to travel regularly within FSM states, including to remote island communities.

Desired Qualifications:

Familiarity with GEF, UNDP, or other multilateral environmental fund requirements and procedures.
Experience with community-based natural resource management, biodiversity conservation, climate resilience, or related thematic areas.
Experience designing or applying monitoring and evaluation frameworks for development or conservation programs.
Demonstrated cultural competency and experience engaging with Indigenous communities and traditional governance structures in Micronesia or the broader Pacific.

What We Bring:

MCT is a world-class conservation trust, the smallest organization to be accredited by the Green Climate Fund and the Adaptation Fund, and it manages over $50 million in assets. We offer a competitive, comprehensive salary and benefits package.

How to Apply:

Qualified candidates are invited to submit the following:
A cover letter (maximum two pages) addressing their qualifications and suitability for the position.
A current curriculum vitae.
Contact information for three professional references.
A brief writing sample (maximum five pages) demonstrating relevant analytical or reporting experience.

Address your application to Melanie Aiseam, CFOO, and email all documents to Lovelynn at
ledgar@ourmicronesia.org by 5:00 pm Pohnpei Time (UTC+11) on September 25, 2026. Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.

This exciting opportunity is designed for individuals who are actively completing coursework to become a BCBA and are accruing practicum hours. Struggling to get opportunities that count toward your unrestricted hours? Looking for a role where you can get paid while building the clinical skills needed to become a BCBA? This role is for you.

The Case Supervisor role is intended to help you develop the foundational skills needed to become a successful BCBA, while receiving structured supervision, coaching, and hands-on clinical experience. This role reports to the Local Clinical Trainer, who is a BCBA, at your assigned clinic.

role is designed for practicum students who are earlier in their BCBA journey and are generally more than 6–9 months away from completing requirements to become a BCBA. This role has the opportunity for promotion to Lead Case Supervisor when you are within 6 months of testing!

Base pay: $22.50 - $27.00/hour. The initial offer hourly pay will be between $22.50 - $23.75.
Serve as a case supervisor for 1-3 client cases (10 paid unrestricted hours/week), learning and practicing the key skills to become a high-quality BCBA. This is a full-time hourly, position.
Receive dedicated supervision, training, and feedback from your Local Clinical Trainer and other BCBAs in your center
Participate in Apex learning and development opportunities
Build clinical skills through exposure to ESDM, interdisciplinary care, family guidance, assessment, and behavior intervention planning
Join a supportive community of future BCBAs across Soar
Work in a culture that lives out our values: high expectations, collaboration, and fun

Job Responsibilities

As a Case Supervisor, you will:

Serve as a case supervisor for client cases, with scope determined by center needs, clinical readiness, and program progress
Accrue paid unrestricted hours through client programming, supervision, family guidance, assessment, and other BCBA-aligned responsibilities
Update client goals and programming using Soar’s electronic data collection platform
Provide support and supervision to RBTs, with coaching and feedback from BCBAs
Participate in ESDM-specific trainings to grow your clinical skillset
Learn to develop Behavior Intervention Plans using approaches such as Practical Functional Assessment and Skill-Based Treatment
Support family treatment guidance meetings using Soar’s in-house curriculum
Assist with assessments and reassessments for clients, including exposure to tools such as the Vineland, QABF, FAST, and ESDM Curriculum Checklist
Receive coaching and feedback from your Local Clinical Trainer, Partner Clinician, and other BCBAs in your clinic
Participate in interdisciplinary collaboration with Speech-Language Pathologists, Occupational Therapists, Psychologists, and other members of the integrated care team
Provide direct client therapy as part of your full-time role, with the weekly mix of direct therapy and unrestricted activities determined by center needs and program progress

Qualifications

Must be enrolled in or recently completed a Master’s program in ABA or a related field that meets BCBA coursework requirements
You must be at least in your second semester of your master’s or certificate program

Actively accruing practicum hours toward BCBA certification
Demonstrated ability to build rapport and trust with children and families
Emerging skills in case conceptualization, client programming, and clinical planning
Emerging skills in coaching and supporting RBTs
Strong desire to learn, grow, and receive feedback

Interest in growing into a future BCBA role

This position is located in the Case Management Services division of the District of Columbia Department of Corrections (DOC), Central Detention Facility (CDF/DC Jail) and Correctional Treatment Facility (CTF). Case Management Services is responsible for the development of a planned program of institutional activities designed to meet the varied demands, individual needs and abilities of the inmates in DOC custody.

Duties And Responsibilities

CS-09

Provides management, guidance, and evaluation of assigned caseload. Conducts intake interviews with newly admitted inmates in assigned area to obtain pertinent data, and to orient inmates to the institutional rules, regulations, procedures and program opportunities. Conducts Risk and Needs assessment in order to help inmates to identify goals they want to achieve; and during incarceration, help inmates connect with relevant community service providers.

Gathers information from new inmates within 72 hours of admission in order to conduct classification to determine the custody level of the inmates according to their respective charges. Reclassifies inmates every 90 days to ensure the correct classification/custody level is maintained. Recommends programming identified for pre-release inmates that are designed to assist with readjustment to life in the community. Refers inmates to therapeutic services, including but not limited to, stress management, life skills, substance use and anger management programs, while still incarcerated.

CS-11

Develops and implements a planned program of institutional activities designed to meet the varied demands, individual needs, and abilities of an assigned caseload of inmates. Provides management, guidance, and evaluation of assigned caseload. Prepares and when required, presents reports based on observed inmate behavior, conformity to jail policies and procedures, and other evaluative outcomes. Identifies and assesses significant factors or variables in the inmate’s history that may have contributed to criminal behavior.

Considers and evaluates such factors as educational background, family relationships, socioeconomic factors prior to arrest history, substance abuse and where applicable, physical/mental status, etc. Develops a program designed to meet/challenge the inmate during the period of incarceration, with the goal of rehabilitation in thinking, behavior, and outlook. The Micronesia Conservation Trust (MCT) is a non-governmental, non-profit conservation finance organization established to provide sustainable financing for conservation and community development across Micronesia. MCT has a 24-year institutional history and serves as a regional hub for conservation finance across the Federated States of Micronesia (FSM), Palau, the Republic of the Marshall Islands, and the broader Micronesian sub-region.

Under an agreement with the United Nations Development Program (UNDP), MCT has been contracted to serve as the National Host Institution (NHI) for the Global Environment Facility (GEF) Small Grants Program (SGP) in the FSM. The SGP supports civil society organizations and community groups to implement projects that address global environmental challenges – including biodiversity loss, land degradation, climate change, and threats to international waters – in ways that enhance local livelihoods and community well-being.

What We Can Achieve Together:

The Small Grants Programme Manager is responsible for the effective, transparent, and accountable
implementation of the GEF SGP in the FSM. The Manager will ensure that grant resources are directed to eligible, high-impact projects; that grantee organizations are adequately supported throughout the project cycle; and that program results are documented and reported in accordance with UNDP/GEF requirements.

We’re Looking for You:

MCT is seeking to recruit a qualified and experienced Small Grants Program Manager to lead the day-to-day implementation of the SGP-FSM. This role will be based in Chuuk State and will work closely with MCT leadership, a national technical review body, UNDP, GEF, and community stakeholders across the FSM.

What You’ll Bring:

Bachelor’s degree in environmental science, natural resource management, development studies, public administration, or a related field. A Master’s degree is an advantage.
Minimum of five (5) years of professional experience in program or project management, preferably in grant-making, conservation, or community development.
Demonstrated experience in grants management, including proposal review, due diligence, contracting, disbursement tracking, and reporting.
Experience working with or within civil society organizations, government agencies, or international development organizations in the Pacific Islands region.
Strong written and oral communication skills in English; proficiency in a Micronesian language is an advantage.
Demonstrated proficiency in financial management and basic accounting practices related to grant administration.
Ability to travel regularly within FSM states, including to remote island communities.

Desired Qualifications:

Familiarity with GEF, UNDP, or other multilateral environmental fund requirements and procedures.
Experience with community-based natural resource management, biodiversity conservation, climate resilience, or related thematic areas.
Experience designing or applying monitoring and evaluation frameworks for development or conservation programs.
Demonstrated cultural competency and experience engaging with Indigenous communities and traditional governance structures in Micronesia or the broader Pacific.

What We Bring:

MCT is a world-class conservation trust, the smallest organization to be accredited by the Green Climate Fund and the Adaptation Fund, and it manages over $50 million in assets. We offer a competitive, comprehensive salary and benefits package.

Qualified candidates are invited to submit the following:
A cover letter (maximum two pages) addressing their qualifications and suitability for the position.
A current curriculum vitae.
Contact information for three professional references.
A brief writing sample (maximum five pages) demonstrating relevant analytical or reporting experience.

ledgar@ourmicronesia.org by 5:00 pm Pohnpei Time (UTC+11) on September 25, 2026. Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.
